subject: Consolidated add-on pricing: staircase rebate proposal for retention + tracing + dashboards
messages:
From: Aisha Rao <aisha@vectorone.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: VectorOne Procurement <procurement@vectorone.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Observability add-on pricing — sample usage attached

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. VectorOne is interested in standardizing on Redwood for inference, but the pricing for the observability add-ons (retention, tracing, advanced dashboards) is the last piece blocking the internal approval.

Attached is a 30-day sample of our telemetry footprint (vectorone_usage_snapshot.csv). High-level asks from our side:
- A single blended path we can commit to for year‑1 without having to model three separate surcharges.
- A clear concession path if we exceed baseline ingestion during peak product launches.
- An option for a pilot discount (proof-of-value period) that can convert to credits against committed spend.

We prefer credits that scale (not a flat %), because our retained GBs spike unpredictably. Can Redwood propose something that avoids per-GB sticker shock while giving us visibility into long-term unit economics?

Target deadline for procurement: end of Q1 (we need final commercial terms to route for legal).

Thanks,
Aisha Rao
Head of Platform Ops, VectorOne
procurement@vectorone.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Aisha Rao <aisha@vectorone.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Observability add-on pricing — sample usage attached

Ben / Kim — looping you in. VectorOne sent a usage snapshot and asked for a blended, low‑shock price path plus a pilot credit model. Id like to propose a "staircase rebate" construct:

- Baseline slab (committed GBs/month) priced at X per GB.
- Stair steps: each higher slab triggers an incremental rebate (% of the marginal add-on charge) to soften burst cost.
- Pilot: 8‑week pilot with 50% credits on advanced dashboards and 30% credits on retention/tracing, convertible to credits against year‑1 committed add-on spend if they hit conversion thresholds.

Advantages: predictable baseline, automatic mitigation for bursts, convertible pilot credits that feed the committed invoice. Risks to review: accounting treatment of credits, legal language for conversion, and a cap for extremely long bursts.

Can you draft a matrix and an example invoice for VectorOne showing a 6 month and 12 month conversion path? I attached a skeleton workbook (redwood_addon_staircase_proposal_v1.xlsx). Aisha, well target a short SOW for the pilot and put conversion mechanics into a commercial addendum.

Timing: if we can get Bens matrix today, Ill present to Aisha tomorrow and push to legal.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Director, Commercial GTM
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Mar 29, 2027 at 18:03 Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Can you draft a matrix and an example invoice for VectorOne showing a 6 month and 12 month conversion path?

Attached is a pricing matrix and two sample invoices (tabs: matrix / invoice_6m / invoice_12m). Summary below.

Proposal (summary):
- Baseline slab: commit to 12TB/month retention+trace ingest (slab A) at $0.045/GB effective unit charge.
- Staircase rebates on marginal usage: +5% rebate for slab B (12-24TB), +10% rebate for slab C (24-48TB), +15% rebate for slab D (>48TB). Rebates apply only to the marginal GBs above each threshold.
- Dashboards: seat + feature fee remains separate but pilot credits apply to the feature fee line (50% during pilot).
- Pilot conversion mechanics: if VectorOne converts within 90 days of pilot end, they receive credit equal to 60% of pilot discounts applied, on net 12 month committed add-on spend.
- Burst cap: to protect Redwood economics, rebates stop after sustained >3x baseline for more than two consecutive months; overage then billed at a reduced premium (1.2x baseline rate) — this is negotiable.

Practical example included: month with 30TB ingest shows blended effective price goes from $0.045 to $0.037/GB after rebates. The 6 month and 12 month invoices show how pilot credit amortization flows into month 1 after conversion.

Open items for legal/finance:
- Exact phrasing for "convertible pilot credit" and whether credits offset tickets/overages.
- How to report credits on monthly invoices (line item vs negative invoice).

Next steps: Logan to present to Aisha, Kimberly to draft SOW with Naomi. Im available for a quick call if VectorOne wants to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_addon_staircase_proposal_v1.xlsx (pricing matrix, 2.1MB)
From: Aisha Rao <aisha@vectorone.com>

Subject: Re: Observability add-on pricing — sample usage attached

Thanks Logan / Ben — the matrix is helpful and the staircase rebate concept addresses our main concern about spike exposure. A few quick asks before we move to legal: 

1) Can we shorten the pilot to 6 weeks (we have a tight product launch) and keep the same credit economics pro‑rata?
2) Please confirm that pilot credits only reduce the add-on line and cannot be applied to base inference token fees (our CFO wants this spelled out).
3) Wed like the burst cap threshold softened (3x baseline is high given our launch cadence). Would Redwood consider 4x with a 2.5x soft warning band and automatic alerting integration?

If you can send a 1‑page SOW cover note plus an updated sample invoice reflecting the 6‑week pilot and the credit-isolation clause, procurement can route this to legal today. Wed like to start the pilot first week of May.

Appreciate the quick turn.

—Aisha
Aisha Rao
Head of Platform Ops, VectorOne
